messages.author: 417414441a0ca1d9
messages.subject: Re: New rApache branding
parts:
Jeff, I think you should stick to software. ;)

More seriously, rapache is an unfortunate choice for a name, because
there's another thing out there called rapache (a remote admin interface
for apache).

I see that back in 2005, you wrote the following. Do you still view
these terms this way?

mod_R is a project dedicated to embedding the R interpreter inside
the Apache 2.0 (and beyond) web server for the purpose of writing web
applications in R. It's composed of three parts:

mod_R: the Apache 2.0 module that implements the glue to load the
R interpreter.

RApache: the R package that provides the API for programming web
applications in R.

On Tue, Aug 17, 2010 at 9:42 AM, Jack Tanner <ih...@hotmail.com> wrote:
> Jeff, I think you should stick to software. ;)

I know! It's like I have the desire to create good visual design, but
I just can't get it the way I think it should be, and it usually ends
up sucking. Now, head on over to the wiki and "FIX IT"!

> More seriously, rapache is an unfortunate choice for a name, because
> there's another thing out there called rapache (a remote admin interface
> for apache).

Yeah, but I think that the original rapache is dead:

http://www.stefanoforenza.com/rapache-on-ubuntu-10-04-not-likely/

> I see that back in 2005, you wrote the following. Do you still view
> these terms this way?
>
>    mod_R is a project dedicated to embedding the R interpreter inside
>    the Apache 2.0 (and beyond) web server for the purpose of writing web
>    applications in R. It's composed of three parts:
>
>    mod_R: the Apache 2.0 module that implements the glue to load the
>    R interpreter.
>
>    RApache: the R package that provides the API for programming web
>    applications in R.

Well, sort of. There's no longer an rApache R package. The
functionality, e.g., access to the CGI and server variables has been
"magically" embedded into the R runtime.

Jeff
